newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firms as crude pares losses.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firms as crude pares losses.

text.p: NWE gasoline was flat to slightly stronger in afternoon trade on Monday as crude prices pared some of the losses they posted on Friday and trading activity picked up, traders said.
Eurograde barges traded at least twice at $190 and once $191 fob ARA throughout the day.
Regular barges, meanwhile, traded at $180 and $185 fob ARA during the session.
Some players expressed scepticism about the $180 deal speculating that the players involved were trying to lower quotes ahead of a delivery into the region.
Traders attributed earlier losses to dramatic falls in crude prices late on Friday after much of the market had packed up for the day.
The May IPE Brent contract fell as low as $17.65 per barrel in the final hour of Friday's session, but was trading 37 cents higher at $18.05 at 1712 GMT.
"Crude's up a bit which has helped gasoline in the afternoon," one trader said.
April swaps were done at $193.25 in afternoon trade and were quoted around the $193.50/$194.50 level, while May paper was quoted around the $195/$196 level.
Traders said the supply situation in the region remained fairly sloppy, especially with the arbitrage door to the United States firmly shut.
They also noted that rising margins due to the fall in crude was increasing supply as refiners maximised production.
Shell Rotterdam, for example, was reported to have restored its refinery to full production. It had been running some 12-15 percent below capacity since March 4.
Last complex refiners in the ARA region saw margins improve by 25 percent to over $2.50 a barrel, from an average of $2.04 in the last week in March.
